faqs.q: What are Counterweight Lifting Beams used for?
faqs.a: Counterweight lifting beams hold the load at the end of a cantilever, with a counterweight on the other side of the top lift point to balance it. The crane hook stays clear of the structure while the load goes in under a roof, onto a mezzanine or through a window opening.

faqs.q: What is the part number for Counterweight Lifting Beams?
faqs.a: IH-LR-BH-CWB is the base part number for Counterweight Lifting Beams. Each beam is made to order from an approved general arrangement drawing, so send the load data and we confirm the exact part number and design with the quotation.

faqs.q: What sizes and capacities do Counterweight Lifting Beams come in?
faqs.a: Counterweight Lifting Beams are built to the load, with the working load limit and size set to order rather than from a size table. Send the load weight and where its centre of gravity sits, the load’s length and width, the lifting point positions, the crane hook height and any headroom limit, and the environment (indoor, outdoor, offshore, hazardous area) and the maker’s design engineers issue a general arrangement drawing for your approval before anything is made.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right design of Counterweight Lifting Beams?
faqs.a: Choose a fixed counterweight for one load and an adjustable counterweight for a range of loads. Precast versions place wall and floor units under an existing structure. Send the load and the opening so the beam can be designed for it.

faqs.q: What is the rated load of Counterweight Lifting Beams?
faqs.a: The working load limit of Counterweight Lifting Beams is set to order for your load, and the rated load, identification and test date are marked on the beam. The user instructions state how it may and may not be rigged; work only to the marked rated load.

faqs.q: What material and finish do Counterweight Lifting Beams have?
faqs.a: Counterweight Lifting Beams are made from structural steel in a grade chosen by the design, with a paint system to your specification. Galvanizing is available for outdoor use on request; state it on the enquiry.

faqs.q: What standard are Counterweight Lifting Beams designed to?
faqs.a: Counterweight Lifting Beams are designed to EN 13155, with ASME B30.20 / BTH-1 or DNV offshore design available on request. Each is load tested before dispatch and supplied with a declaration of conformity, a test certificate and user instructions; design calculations and witnessed testing can be added to the order.

faqs.q: What rigging do Counterweight Lifting Beams need?
faqs.a: Rig the beam from its top lift point and attach the load at the cantilever end as the design shows; the user instructions state how it may be rigged. Shackles and slings are sized to the drawing, and the counterweight is fixed or adjustable as ordered.

faqs.q: How are Counterweight Lifting Beams inspected in service?
faqs.a: Give Counterweight Lifting Beams a pre-use check before every lift and a thorough examination by a competent person at the interval your site authority sets. See our [lifting equipment inspection guide](/blog/lifting-equipment-inspection-uae) and the [centre of gravity in lifting guide](/blog/centre-of-gravity-in-lifting) for planning the lift.

faqs.q: What are typical builds of Counterweight Lifting Beams?
faqs.a: Typical uses are placing loads under canopies and onto mezzanines, installing plant through openings, placing precast units under an existing structure and glazing and cladding units. See the [centre of gravity in lifting guide](/blog/centre-of-gravity-in-lifting).

faqs.q: How do Counterweight Lifting Beams differ from the nearest beam type?
faqs.a: A counterweight beam reaches past the hook to place a load under a structure, while a [Fixed Lifting Beams](/p/fixed-lifting-beams) hangs the load from a single top point under the hook. Choose counterweight when the hook cannot reach the placing position.

faqs.q: What are Fixed Lifting Beams used for?

faqs.q: What is the Multi-Configuration Modular Lifting Beam?
faqs.a: It is one beam system that works as several lifting tools: standard sections bolt together to length, and adaptors turn the assembly into a lifting beam, an under beam, a semi-spreader with two top lugs or an H-frame with a cross beam. When the lift changes, the beam is reconfigured on site rather than replaced.

faqs.q: How do I read the part number IH-LR-BH-MCB-16-LB-010?
faqs.a: IH-LR-BH-MCB-16-LB-010 is the modular beam row for a lifting beam (LB) at a 1 m span, and the same pattern gives UB for the under beam and HF2 for the two-top-lug H-frame, with the last block giving the span. The size table lists every configuration and span with its rating.

faqs.q: What spans and configurations does the modular lifting beam cover?
faqs.a: Spans run from 1 to 10 m in sections of 1 m, 2 m and 4 m, and the configurations are lifting beam, under beam, semi-spreader and H-frame, with an H-frame cross beam of 1 to 4 m. The table has 95 configuration and span rows.

faqs.q: What is the rated load of the modular lifting beam at different spans?
faqs.a: The rated load falls as the span grows: a lifting beam or under beam is 16 t at 1–3 m and 2 t at 10 m, a semi-spreader on 4 bottom points is 23 t at 4–6 m and 5 t on 2 bottom points at 10 m, and an H-frame with two top lugs is 16 t at 1 m × 1 m. Work to the table for your configuration.

faqs.q: How does the number of bottom points change the semi-spreader rating?
faqs.a: For a semi-spreader the load shares across two, three or four bottom points, and the rating rises with the number of points. At a 10 m span, for example, the table gives 7 t on 3 bottom points and 5 t on 2 bottom points.

faqs.q: How heavy are the sections and adaptors of the modular beam?
faqs.a: A 1 m section weighs 180 kg, a 2 m section 250 kg and a 4 m section 425 kg, and the under-beam adaptor weighs 31 kg. The beam is made of steel, bolted standard sections and adaptors.

faqs.q: What standard and documents come with the modular lifting beam?
faqs.a: The modular beam is designed to EN 13155 and supplied with a declaration of conformity and user instructions with load tables. Design calculations and witnessed testing can be added to the order.

faqs.q: What shackles does the modular lifting beam use?
faqs.a: Lifting beam spans of 1–3 m use 9.5 t super-bow bottom shackles and 6.5 t standard bow shackles from 4 m. An under beam takes an 8.5 t shackle at the central bolt hole or 17 t at the bolt-on lugs, and an H-frame with a single top lug takes one 17 t top shackle.

faqs.q: How are modular lifting beams inspected in service?
faqs.a: Give the beam a pre-use check before every lift and a thorough examination by a competent person at the interval your site authority sets. See our [lifting equipment inspection guide](/blog/lifting-equipment-inspection-uae) and the [centre of gravity in lifting guide](/blog/centre-of-gravity-in-lifting).

faqs.q: Can the modular lifting beam be set up for other lifts?
faqs.a: Yes. Adaptors also make counterweight beams, fork-pocket beams and low-height lifting frames, so tell us the lift and we confirm whether the beam can be configured for it and at what rating. See the [spreader beam vs lifting beam guide](/blog/spreader-beam-vs-lifting-beam).

faqs.q: Modular lifting beam or a fixed made-to-order beam?
faqs.a: The modular beam is reconfigured on site, while a [Fixed Lifting Beams](/p/fixed-lifting-beams) is built to one load. Use the modular system when lifts vary; use a fixed beam for a heavy one-off.

faqs.q: Is the modular lifting beam available to order from Dubai?
faqs.a: The modular beam is a made-to-order system and the availability note says: Contact us for current lead time. Send the load, its lifting points and your headroom through [our contact page](/contact).
